title: Long Jumps
statementMd:
Valery is a PE teacher at a school in Berland. Soon the students are going to take a test in long jumps, and Valery has lost his favorite ruler!

However, there is no reason for disappointment, as Valery has found another ruler, its length is $*l*$ centimeters. The ruler already has $*n*$ marks, with which he can make measurements. We assume that the marks are numbered from 1 to $*n*$ in the order they appear from the beginning of the ruler to its end. The first point coincides with the beginning of the ruler and represents the origin. The last mark coincides with the end of the ruler, at distance $*l*$ from the origin. This ruler can be repesented by an increasing sequence $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$, where $*a*_{*i*}$ denotes the distance of the $*i*$-th mark from the origin ($*a*_{1} = 0$, $*a*_{*n*} = *l*$).

Valery believes that with a ruler he can measure the distance of $*d*$ centimeters, if there is a pair of integers $*i*$ and $*j*$ ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ *j* ≤ *n*$), such that the distance between the $*i*$-th and the $*j*$-th mark is exactly equal to $*d*$ (in other words, $*a*_{*j*} - *a*_{*i*} = *d*$).

Under the rules, the girls should be able to jump at least $*x*$ centimeters, and the boys should be able to jump at least $*y*$ ($*x* < *y*$) centimeters. To test the children's abilities, Valery needs a ruler to measure each of the distances $*x*$ and $*y*$.

Your task is to determine what is the minimum number of additional marks you need to add on the ruler so that they can be used to measure the distances $*x*$ and $*y*$. Valery can add the marks at any integer non-negative distance from the origin not exceeding the length of the ruler.

## Input

The first line contains four positive space-separated integers $*n*$, $*l*$, $*x*$, $*y*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $2 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{9}$, $1 ≤ *x* < *y* ≤ *l*$) — the number of marks, the length of the ruler and the jump norms for girls and boys, correspondingly.

The second line contains a sequence of $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($0 = *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} = *l*$), where $*a*_{*i*}$ shows the distance from the $*i*$-th mark to the origin.

## Output

In the first line print a single non-negative integer $*v*$ — the minimum number of marks that you need to add on the ruler.

In the second line print $*v*$ space-separated integers $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*v*}$ ($0 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *l*$). Number $*p*_{*i*}$ means that the $*i*$-th mark should be at the distance of $*p*_{*i*}$ centimeters from the origin. Print the marks in any order. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

## Note

In the first sample it is impossible to initially measure the distance of $230$ centimeters. For that it is enough to add a $20$ centimeter mark or a $230$ centimeter mark.

In the second sample you already can use the ruler to measure the distances of $185$ and $230$ centimeters, so you don't have to add new marks.

In the third sample the ruler only contains the initial and the final marks. We will need to add two marks to be able to test the children's skills.
statementZhMd:
瓦列里是别尔兰一所学校的体育老师。学生们很快就要参加跳远测试了，而瓦列里弄丢了他最喜欢的尺子！

不过，没有必要失望，因为瓦列里找到了另一把尺子，其长度为 $*l*$ 厘米。这把尺子上已经有 $*n*$ 个刻度，可以用来进行测量。我们假设这些刻度按照它们从尺子起点到终点出现的顺序编号为 1 到 $*n*$。第一个刻度与尺子的起点重合，表示原点。最后一个刻度与尺子的终点重合，它到原点的距离为 $*l*$。这把尺子可以表示为一个递增序列 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$，其中 $*a*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 个刻度到原点的距离（$*a*_{1} = 0$，$*a*_{*n*} = *l*$）。

瓦列里认为，如果存在一对整数 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *j* ≤ *n*$），使得第 $*i*$ 个刻度和第 $*j*$ 个刻度之间的距离恰好等于 $*d*$（换句话说，$*a*_{*j*} - *a*_{*i*} = *d*$），那么他就可以用尺子测量出 $*d*$ 厘米的距离。

按照规定，女生至少应能跳 $*x*$ 厘米，男生至少应能跳 $*y*$ 厘米（$*x* < *y*$）。为了测试孩子们的能力，瓦列里需要一把能够测量 $*x*$ 和 $*y*$ 这两个距离的尺子。

你的任务是确定至少需要在尺子上增加多少个刻度，才能用它测量出 $*x*$ 和 $*y*$。瓦列里可以在距原点任意非负整数距离处增加刻度，但该距离不能超过尺子的长度。

## 输入

第一行包含四个用空格分隔的正整数 $*n*$、$*l*$、$*x*$、$*y*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$2 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{9}$，$1 ≤ *x* < *y* ≤ *l*$）——刻度的数量、尺子的长度，以及女生和男生的跳远标准。

第二行包含一个由 $*n*$ 个整数组成的序列 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$0 = *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} = *l*$），其中 $*a*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 个刻度到原点的距离。

## 输出

第一行输出一个非负整数 $*v*$——需要在尺子上增加的最少刻度数。

第二行输出 $*v*$ 个用空格分隔的整数 $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*v*}$（$0 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *l*$）。数字 $*p*_{*i*}$ 表示应在距原点 $*p*_{*i*}$ 厘米处增加第 $*i*$ 个刻度。刻度可以按任意顺序输出。如果有多种方案，输出任意一种即可。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，原本无法测量 $230$ 厘米的距离。只需增加一个位于 $20$ 厘米处或 $230$ 厘米处的刻度即可。

在第二个样例中，已经可以用尺子测量出 $185$ 厘米和 $230$ 厘米的距离，因此不需要增加新的刻度。

在第三个样例中，尺子只包含起点和终点两个刻度。为了能够测试孩子们的能力，需要增加两个刻度。
